title: Dynamic Zoom for a gentle push-in or pull-out
note: On the Edit page, select the timeline clip and enable Dynamic Zoom in the Inspector. The viewer shows green starting-frame and red ending-frame boxes; adjust their framing and play to review the movement. This method is intended for a simple automated push or pull rather than a custom keyframed camera path.

title: Animating position, scale and rotation
note: On the Edit page, select a timeline clip and open the Inspector. Adjust position, scale, or rotation and activate the diamond-shaped keyframe control for that parameter; move the playhead and change the parameter again to define the motion. The timeline's keyframe and curve controls can refine timing and easing.

title: Stabilizing shaky footage
note: The Edit page Inspector has a Stabilization section for reducing unwanted camera movement. Available settings described by Blackmagic include smoothing, strength, crop ratio, camera lock and zooming. Select the clip, choose suitable stabilization settings, run Stabilize, and inspect the result to avoid unnatural cropping or motion.

title: Basic color correction with primary color wheels
note: The Color page primary controls offer Lift, Gamma and Gain for shadows, midtones and highlights, while Offset affects the whole image. Use them to establish balanced exposure and color before applying a creative look. Keep stylized source footage consistent rather than blindly aiming for photographic realism.

title: Layering effects with Fusion nodes
note: In Fusion, effects are built as connected nodes. A Merge node composites a foreground (green input) onto a background (yellow input); insert effect nodes into the flow and use masks to limit an effect to an area. The Inspector controls a selected tool, with Spline and Keyframes panels available for animation adjustments.

title: Exporting a finished edit
note: Blackmagic describes File > Quick Export as a short path to common delivery options. For specialized export settings and reusable presets, switch to the Deliver page. Confirm resolution, frame rate, codec and output location match the intended platform before rendering.

title: Adjusting clip audio and mixing tracks
note: The Edit page supports adjusting individual audio clip levels in the timeline or in the Inspector. Use the mixer track faders to balance entire tracks, and the audio meters to avoid levels that are too quiet or loud. Fairlight provides more extensive processing for dialogue, sound effects and music.
